Night Work work executed between 18:00 and 06:00.

Rest day Friday and Saturday.

A record required by Schedule 5 shall identify the work area, the date, the item code and the quantity, and shall be signed by the Subcontractor's foreman and countersigned by the Engineer's representative.
The record is written in the words of the person who did the work and does not repeat the description in Schedule 1.
A record covering a week records each day worked. A week is measurable only where the record shows work on not fewer than five days of that week (Clause 47A).
A site record is written by the person who carried out the work and is not required to adopt the wording of the Bill of Quantities.
A record that evidences a week records each day worked; a week is measurable only where the record shows work on not fewer than five days of that week.
4. **Every line has its record** for that day or run, signed by whoever the contract says signs it.

discrepancies: Label: validation case 3 attributes the 'record wording differs from the BoQ description' point to the 'Sch 5 note'; on p27 that wording is in the Schedule 5 introductory paragraph above the table ('The record is written in the words of the person who did the work and does not repeat the description in Schedule 1'), while the note below the table is the weekly-record/five-day note. The point itself is also in 47A (p33). Substance is supported. Not in the text (interpretation, not contradicted): validation 1 - neither 47A nor the Sch 5 note mentions weeks that cross a month boundary; they say only that a weekly record records each day worked, so how such a week is split between applications is left open. Validation 2 - the text supports that the record must identify the date (Cl.47), but classifying a date difference as a 'mismatch fact kept separate from reuse and duplication' is an analyst choice; Cl.44 (duplicate measurement, p8) is a separate clause and says nothing about date mismatch; 'Q7' is an internal reference not checkable against the contract. Title omits Cl.47's signature/countersignature requirement (not a claim, noted only). Cl.47 applies to 'A record required by Schedule 5', which matches the scope 'lines with a record' only for Sch 5 items.

quotes.text: Where an item is measured by the hour, a Chargeable Hour is an hour of attendance other than the first hour of that attendance. The site record states the hours attended; the quantity measured is one hour fewer.

Where an item is measured against a joint survey, a measured quantity not exceeding the surveyed quantity by more than 2 per cent is payable as measured. A measured quantity exceeding the surveyed quantity by more than that is payable at the surveyed quantity only.
A record that evidences a week records each day worked; a week is measurable only where the record shows work on not fewer than five days of that week.
Items marked as surveyed in Schedule 1 are measured only against a joint survey sheet signed by both parties. The quantity measured shall be the quantity on the survey sheet exactly.
Part 6 — Surveyed items The following items are measured only against a joint survey sheet signed by both parties (Clause 33).
Setting out is measured under item E.52.010 by chainage band and only against a joint survey signed by both parties.
Wastage on reinforcement is deemed included. The quantity measured is the theoretical mass on the approved bar schedule (Clause 33).
5. **The quantities are the recorded ones.** Billed above the record is payable up to the record, not at all above it.

discrepancies: No contradicted claim. Arithmetic checked: 102.00% exceeds the survey by exactly 2 per cent, i.e. not by more than 2 per cent, so payable as measured (33A); 102.01% exceeds by more than 2 per cent, so surveyed quantity only; 4 days < 'not fewer than five' so the week is not measurable (47A); 1 hour attended - 1 = 0 chargeable (6A). Parameter values 1 / 5 / 2 match 6A 'first hour', 47A 'five days', 33A '2 per cent'. Ambiguities (described, not resolved): (a) Cl.33 (p7) says the quantity measured 'shall be the quantity on the survey sheet exactly', while 33A (p32) allows up to 2 per cent above the survey to be paid as measured; the text does not state which prevails (Cl.2 on p3 ranks Schedules over General Conditions but says nothing of the Particular Conditions). (b) Guideline check 5 says billed above the record is payable 'not at all above it', whereas 33A pays up to 2 per cent above a joint survey as measured - the contract governs, so validation cases 1 and 5 differ for surveyed items. (c) Validation case 6 (billed below the record payable as billed, never raised) is not stated in the contract or guideline check 5, which addresses only billing above the record; 33A's 'not exceeding ... is payable as measured' is consistent with it for surveyed items, but Cl.33's 'exactly' could be read otherwise. 'Q10' is an internal reference not checkable against the contract. P18 (p13) makes the reinforcement quantity the theoretical mass on the approved bar schedule, cross-referring to Clause 33. 'Sch 4 Part 6' label: Part 6 is on p26 under Schedule 4 (Schedule 4 heading on p24 per OCR; P19 on p13 cites 'Schedule 4, Part 5', which is on p26).

quotes.text: Trench depth shall be measured from the existing ground level at the centre line of the trench to the invert of the pipe, and shall determine which of items A.12.020, A.12.030 and A.12.040 applies. Where a single trench spans two depth bands each part shall be measured separately.
A.12.020 Excavation in trench, depth not exceeding 2 m m3 2,675 34.80
A.12.030 Excavation in trench, depth 2 m to 4 m m3 575 47.60
A.12.040 Excavation in trench, depth exceeding 4 m m3 900 69.20
Series C — Drainage and Ducting
Rates are per unit stated. No item may be measured in a unit other than the one shown (Clause 26).
6. **Each line is identified** against a priced item; where two could fit, leave it unresolved rather than choose on price.

discrepancies: No contradicted claim. Ambiguity (described, not resolved): the Sch 1 depth bands as printed overlap at exactly 2 m - A.12.020 'depth not exceeding 2 m' and A.12.030 'depth 2 m to 4 m' both include 2 m; at 4 m, A.12.030 'depth 2 m to 4 m' includes it and A.12.040 'depth exceeding 4 m' does not. P13 does not say which band a depth of exactly 2 m falls in. The 'unresolved, never cheapest' validation rests on guideline check 6 ('rather than choose on price'), not on contract text; P13 and Sch 1 do not address unresolvable identification. Pages 18-19 carry the rest of Sch 1 (Series B-E) and contain nothing specific to trench depth.

quotes.text: Provisional sums shall be expended only on the written instruction of the Engineer and shall be omitted from the Subcontract Sum if not so instructed.

Work instructed to be executed on a daywork basis shall be recorded on daywork sheets signed daily by the Engineer's representative. Daywork sheets not signed on the day of the work shall not be admitted.
Work for which no rate appears in Schedule 1 shall be valued at daywork rates in Schedule 6 unless a rate is agreed in writing before the work is executed.

The rates below apply only to work instructed to be executed on a daywork basis under Clause 17, and to work for which no rate appears in Schedule 1 (Clause P24). Daywork sheets shall be signed on the day of the work.
The percentage additions are applied to the net cost and are the only additions allowable. No profit is added separately.
The sums below are included in the Subcontract Sum and shall be expended only on the written instruction of the Engineer (Clause 16). A sum not so instructed shall be omitted.
A provisional sum (PS) covers work not yet defined. A prime cost sum (PC) covers materials to be supplied by others. Neither is measured under Schedule 1.
An item priced against the unit "item" is a fixed charge and is valued once, in the valuation in which the obligation is discharged.
PR.01 Site establishment, offices and welfare item 486,000.00
Preliminaries are not subject to the zone factor, the ground factor, or any uplift or rebate. They are valued at the amounts stated (Clause 29).
3. **Say when you do not know.** An invoice you cannot price is a query. Record what is missing rather than guessing a figure.

discrepancies: No contradicted claim; PR.01 amount 486,000.00 and unit 'item' match p31; Sch 6 on pp28-29 (Part 3 additions: Labour 68%, Plant 22% on p28; Materials 14%, Subcontracted daywork 10% on p29), Sch 7 on p30, Sch 8 on p31, Cl.16/17 on p4, P24 on p14 - labels correct. Ambiguity (described, not resolved): the contract states its own consequence when the condition is not met - daywork sheets not signed on the day 'shall not be admitted' (Cl.17) and a provisional sum not instructed 'shall be omitted' (Cl.16, Sch 7) - which reads as disallowance; the 'query' outcome in the rule comes from guideline principle 3 and applies where the supplied data cannot show whether the condition was met. The text does not distinguish 'no evidence supplied' from 'condition not met'. P24 also allows a rate 'agreed in writing before the work is executed' as an alternative to Sch 6 daywork rates for unrated work. 'Q8' and 'synthetic PR.01 line' refer to the analyst's data/query log and are not checkable against the contract. Sch 7's written-instruction condition covers both provisional (PS) and prime cost (PC) sums; the validation case names only provisional sums.

quotes.text: 12. **The outcome is written down** -- pass, query, or part-reject -- with the clause relied on, the figure you say is payable, and anything you could not determine.
3. **Say when you do not know.** An invoice you cannot price is a query. Record what is missing rather than guessing a figure.
Apply the twelve checks in `INVOICE_AUDIT_GUIDELINES.md` to every invoice under both contracts, and record the outcome for each one in a **single submission file**.
Rows you cannot price are still rows — flag them if you believe they are wrong, give your confidence honestly, and say in your report what you could not determine.

discrepancies: No contradicted claim. Title matches guideline check 12 nearly word for word; the validation case matches guideline principle 3. Observation (not resolved): the README Task records the outcome in a submission file whose columns are flagged (1/0), error_category, expected_total_cents, billed_total_cents and confidence - it has no pass/query/part-reject field and no field for the clause relied on, and expected_total_cents is an integer in minor units ('There are no fractional amounts in a submission'), so an unpriceable row still needs some encoding of its total; the README places 'what you could not determine' in the report. 'Q9' (unknown-total encoding) is an internal reference not checkable against these documents. No contract pages cited or read.
